newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening higher, limited gains.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening higher, limited gains.

text.p: * Toronto stocks were expected to open higher as gold prices and overseas markets strengthened but analysts said gains would be limited as North American bonds were under pressure.
Toronto stocks were expected to rise at the open on Monday but face a choppy day as gold and overseas markets strengthened and North American bonds were under pressure.
"I think we're going to go higher but with bonds under pressure it's not going to be a strong move up," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
She said stronger golds and a firmer Canadian dollar will help boost Toronto's key precious metals and financial sub-indexes, while the overall market should be helped by Friday's record close.
Toronto's key stock index posted a record close for the second consecutive session on Friday, climbing 33.48 points to 6626.40.
Canada's largest equities market also reached a new intraday record of 6633 points, capping a week of gains.
Beattie said the bounce by golds from 12-year lows is likely only a temporary pause in the metal's downtrend.

"I don't the downtrend is over yet, so I think we could get a few days up and then go back down, return to the lows we saw last week around the US$314 (per ounce) area. If $314 can hold on the second test, then I would say the downtrend looks like it is over," Beattie said.
"But the trend is down until proven otherwise -- we've got to look for weakness," she added.
((Andrea Hopkins at Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8102 or e-mail andrea.hopkins@reuters.com))
